app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

- apiVersion: v1
  data:
    relay: "connectors:\n  span_metrics: {}\nexporters:\n  debug: {}\n  opensearch:\n\
      \    http:\n      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200\n      tls:\n        insecure:\
      \ true\n    logs_index: otel-logs\n    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd\n\
      \  otlp_grpc/firepit:\n    endpoint: firepit:4317\n    tls:\n      insecure:\
      \ true\n  otlp_grpc/jaeger:\n    endpoint: jaeger:4317\n    sending_queue:\n\
      \      batch: {}\n    tls:\n      insecure: true\n  otlp_http/prometheus:\n\
      \    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp\n    sending_queue:\n    \
      \  batch: {}\n    tls:\n      insecure: true\nextensions:\n  health_check:\n\
      \    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133\n  k8s_leader_elector/k8s_cluster:\n \
      \   auth_type: serviceAccount\n    lease_name: k8s.cluster.receiver.opentelemetry.io\n\
      \    lease_namespace: astronomy-shop\n  k8s_observer:\n    auth_type: serviceAccount\n\
      \    node: ${env:K8S_NODE_NAME}\n  opamp:\n    agent_description:\n      include_resource_attributes:\
      \ true\n      non_identifying_attributes:\n        demo.collector.role: gateway\n\
      \        deployment.environment.name: demo\n    capabilities:\n      reports_available_components:\
      \ true\n      reports_effective_config: true\n      reports_health: true\n \
      \   instance_uid: 00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000001\n    server:\n      ws:\n\
      \        endpoint: ws://opamp-server:4320/v1/opamp\nprocessors:\n  batch: {}\n\
      \  filter/sanitize_profiles:\n    error_mode: ignore\n    profiles:\n      profile:\n\
      \      - IsMatch(resource.attributes[\"service.name\"], \"containerd-shim-.*\"\
      )\n  gen_ai_normalizer:\n    sources:\n    - name: openllmetry\n  k8s_attributes:\n\
      \    extract:\n      metadata:\n      - k8s.namespace.name\n      - k8s.pod.name\n\
      \      - k8s.pod.uid\n      - k8s.node.name\n      - k8s.pod.start_time\n  \
      \    - k8s.deployment.name\n      - k8s.replicaset.name\n      - k8s.replicaset.uid\n\
      \      - k8s.daemonset.name\n      - k8s.daemonset.uid\n      - k8s.job.name\n\
      \      - k8s.job.uid\n      - k8s.container.name\n      - k8s.cronjob.name\n\
      \      - k8s.statefulset.name\n      - k8s.statefulset.uid\n      - container.image.tag\n\
      \      - container.image.name\n      - k8s.cluster.uid\n      - service.namespace\n\
      \      - service.name\n      - service.version\n      - service.instance.id\n\
      \      otel_annotations: true\n    filter:\n      node_from_env_var: K8S_NODE_NAME\n\
      \    passthrough: false\n    pod_association:\n    - sources:\n      - from:\
      \ resource_attribute\n        name: container.id\n    - sources:\n      - from:\
      \ resource_attribute\n        name: k8s.pod.ip\n    - sources:\n      - from:\
      \ resource_attribute\n        name: k8s.pod.uid\n    - sources:\n      - from:\
      \ connection\n  memory_limiter:\n    check_interval: 5s\n    limit_percentage:\
      \ 80\n    spike_limit_percentage: 25\n  redaction:\n    allow_all_keys: true\n\
      \    blocked_key_patterns:\n    - demo\\.payment\\.card_pin\n    - password\n\
      \    - secret\n    ignored_keys:\n    - demo.payment.card_number\n    summary:\
      \ info\n  resource:\n    attributes:\n    - action: insert\n      from_attribute:\
      \ k8s.pod.uid\n      key: service.instance.id\n  resource_detection:\n    detectors:\n\
      \    - env\n    - system\n  transform/redact_sensitive_data:\n    error_mode:\
      \ ignore\n    trace_statements:\n    - context: span\n      statements:\n  \
      \    - delete_key(attributes, \"demo.payment.card_cvv\") where attributes[\"\
      demo.payment.card_cvv\"]\n        != nil\n      - set(attributes[\"user.hash\"\
      ], SHA256(attributes[\"user.email\"])) where attributes[\"user.email\"]\n  \
      \      != nil\n      - delete_key(attributes, \"user.email\") where attributes[\"\
      user.email\"] != nil\n      - replace_pattern(attributes[\"demo.payment.card_number\"\
      ], \"^\\\\d{4}-\\\\d{4}-\\\\d{4}-\",\n        \"****-****-****-\") where attributes[\"\
      demo.payment.card_number\"] != nil\n  transform/sanitize_logs:\n    error_mode:\
      \ ignore\n    log_statements:\n    - context: scope\n      statements:\n   \
      \   - set(attributes[\"otelcol_signal\"], attributes[\"otelcol.signal\"]) where\
      \ attributes[\"otelcol.signal\"]\n        != nil and not IsMap(attributes[\"\
      otelcol.signal\"])\n      - delete_key(attributes, \"otelcol.signal\") where\
      \ attributes[\"otelcol_signal\"]\n        != nil\n  transform/sanitize_spans:\n\
      \    error_mode: ignore\n    trace_statements:\n    - context: span\n      statements:\n\
      \      - set_semconv_span_name(\"1.43.0\", \"original_span_name\")\nreceivers:\n\
      \  hostmetrics:\n    collection_interval: 10s\n    root_path: /hostfs\n    scrapers:\n\
      \      cpu: null\n      disk: null\n      filesystem:\n        exclude_fs_types:\n\
      \          fs_types:\n          - autofs\n          - binfmt_misc\n        \
      \  - bpf\n          - cgroup2\n          - configfs\n          - debugfs\n \
      \         - devpts\n          - devtmpfs\n          - fusectl\n          - hugetlbfs\n\
      \          - iso9660\n          - mqueue\n          - nsfs\n          - overlay\n\
      \          - proc\n          - procfs\n          - pstore\n          - rpc_pipefs\n\
      \          - securityfs\n          - selinuxfs\n          - squashfs\n     \
      \     - sysfs\n          - tracefs\n          match_type: strict\n        exclude_mount_points:\n\
      \          match_type: regexp\n          mount_points:\n          - ^/dev($|/)\n\
      \          - ^/proc($|/)\n          - ^/sys($|/)\n          - ^/run/k3s/containerd($|/)\n\
      \          - ^/var/lib/docker($|/)\n          - ^/var/lib/kubelet($|/)\n   \
      \       - ^/snap($|/)\n      load: null\n      memory: null\n      network:\
      \ null\n  jaeger:\n    protocols:\n      grpc:\n        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250\n\
      \      thrift_compact:\n        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831\n      thrift_http:\n\
      \        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268\n  k8s_cluster:\n    collection_interval:\
      \ 10s\n    k8s_leader_elector: k8s_leader_elector/k8s_cluster\n  kafkametrics:\n\
      \    brokers:\n    - kafka:9092\n    collection_interval: 10s\n    scrapers:\n\
      \    - brokers\n    - topics\n    - consumers\n  kubeletstats:\n    auth_type:\
      \ serviceAccount\n    collection_interval: 20s\n    endpoint: ${env:K8S_NODE_IP}:10250\n\
      \  otlp:\n    protocols:\n      grpc:\n        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317\n\
      \      http:\n        cors:\n          allowed_headers:\n          - content-type\n\
      \          - traceparent\n          - baggage\n          allowed_origins:\n\
      \          - http://*\n          - https://*\n        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318\n\
      \  prometheus:\n    config:\n      scrape_configs:\n      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector\n\
      \        scrape_interval: 10s\n        static_configs:\n        - targets:\n\
      \          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888\n  prometheus/ad:\n    config:\n      scrape_configs:\n\
      \      - job_name: ad\n        scrape_interval: 10s\n        static_configs:\n\
      \        - targets:\n          - ad:9465\n  receiver_creator/metrics:\n    discovery:\n\
      \      enabled: true\n    watch_observers:\n    - k8s_observer\n  zipkin:\n\
      \    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411\nservice:\n  extensions:\n  - health_check\n\
      \  - opamp\n  - k8s_observer\n  - k8s_leader_elector/k8s_cluster\n  pipelines:\n\
      \    logs:\n      exporters:\n      - opensearch\n      - debug\n      processors:\n\
      \      - k8s_attributes\n      - memory_limiter\n      - resource_detection\n\
      \      - resource\n      - transform/sanitize_logs\n      receivers:\n     \
      \ - otlp\n    metrics:\n      exporters:\n      - otlp_http/prometheus\n   \
      \   - debug\n      processors:\n      - k8s_attributes\n      - memory_limiter\n\
      \      - resource_detection\n      - resource\n      receivers:\n      - otlp\n\
      \      - kafkametrics\n      - span_metrics\n      - prometheus/ad\n      -\
      \ receiver_creator/metrics\n      - hostmetrics\n      - kubeletstats\n    \
      \  - k8s_cluster\n    profiles:\n      exporters:\n      - otlp_grpc/firepit\n\
      \      - debug\n      processors:\n      - k8s_attributes\n      - memory_limiter\n\
      \      - resource_detection\n      - resource\n      - filter/sanitize_profiles\n\
      \      receivers:\n      - otlp\n    traces:\n      exporters:\n      - otlp_grpc/jaeger\n\
      \      - debug\n      - span_metrics\n      processors:\n      - k8s_attributes\n\
      \      - memory_limiter\n      - resource_detection\n      - resource\n    \
      \  - transform/sanitize_spans\n      - gen_ai_normalizer\n      - transform/redact_sensitive_data\n\
      \      - redaction\n      receivers:\n      - otlp\n      - jaeger\n      -\
      \ zipkin\n  telemetry:\n    logs:\n      processors:\n      - batch:\n     \
      \     exporter:\n            otlp:\n              endpoint: http://otel-collector:4318\n\
      \              insecure: true\n              protocol: http/protobuf\n    metrics:\n\
      \      level: detailed\n      readers:\n      - periodic:\n          exporter:\n\
      \            otlp:\n              endpoint: http://otel-collector:4318\n   \
      \           insecure: true\n              protocol: http/protobuf\n        \
      \  interval: 10000\n          timeout: 5000\n    resource:\n      host.name:\
      \ ${env:OTEL_K8S_NODE_NAME}\n      k8s.namespace.name: ${env:OTEL_K8S_NAMESPACE}\n\
      \      k8s.node.ip: ${env:OTEL_K8S_NODE_IP}\n      k8s.node.name: ${env:OTEL_K8S_NODE_NAME}\n\
      \      k8s.pod.ip: ${env:OTEL_K8S_POD_IP}\n      k8s.pod.name: ${env:OTEL_K8S_POD_NAME}\n"

- apiVersion: v1
  data:
    init.sql: "-- Copyright The OpenTelemetry Authors\n-- SPDX-License-Identifier:\
      \ Apache-2.0\n\n-- Enable pg_stat_statements in the default postgres database\n\
      CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements;\n\n-- Create application\
      \ user\nCREATE USER astronomy_user WITH PASSWORD 'astronomy_password';\n\n--\
      \ Create application database\nCREATE DATABASE astronomy_db OWNER astronomy_user;\n\
      \n-- Create monitoring user with pg_monitor role (visibility on all databases\
      \ and schemas)\nCREATE USER monitoring_user WITH PASSWORD 'monitoring_password';\n\
      GRANT pg_monitor TO monitoring_user;\n\n-- Switch to the application database\n\
      \\connect astronomy_db\n\n-- Enable pg_stat_statements in the application database\n\
      CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_stat_statements;\n\n-- Accounting Service:\
      \ create a schema\nCREATE SCHEMA accounting;\nGRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA accounting\
      \ TO astronomy_user;\n\n-- Accounting Service: create tables\nCREATE TABLE accounting.\"\
      order\" (\n    order_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY\n);\n\nCREATE TABLE accounting.shipping\
      \ (\n    shipping_tracking_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n    shipping_cost_currency_code\
      \ TEXT NOT NULL,\n    shipping_cost_units BIGINT NOT NULL,\n    shipping_cost_nanos\
      \ INT NOT NULL,\n    street_address TEXT,\n    city TEXT,\n    state TEXT,\n\
      \    country TEXT,\n    zip_code TEXT,\n    order_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n    FOREIGN\
      \ KEY (order_id) REFERENCES accounting.\"order\"(order_id) ON DELETE CASCADE\n\
      );\n\nCREATE TABLE accounting.orderitem (\n    item_cost_currency_code TEXT\
      \ NOT NULL,\n    item_cost_units BIGINT NOT NULL,\n    item_cost_nanos INT NOT\
      \ NULL,\n    product_id TEXT NOT NULL,\n    quantity INT NOT NULL,\n    order_id\
      \ TEXT NOT NULL,\n    PRIMARY KEY (order_id, product_id),\n    FOREIGN KEY (order_id)\
      \ REFERENCES accounting.\"order\"(order_id) ON DELETE CASCADE\n);\n\n-- Accounting\
      \ Service: grant permission to schema\nGRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON ALL TABLES\
      \ IN SCHEMA accounting TO astronomy_user;\n\n-- Product Catalog Service: create\
      \ a schema\nCREATE SCHEMA catalog;\nGRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA catalog TO astronomy_user;\n\
      \n-- Product Catalog Service: create tables\nCREATE TABLE catalog.products (\n\
      \    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n    name TEXT NOT NULL,\n    description TEXT,\n\
      \    picture TEXT,\n    price_currency_code TEXT NOT NULL,\n    price_units\
      \ BIGINT NOT NULL,\n    price_nanos INT NOT NULL,\n    categories TEXT\n);\n\
      \n-- Product Catalog Service: grant permission to schema\nGRANT SELECT ON ALL\
      \ TABLES IN SCHEMA catalog TO astronomy_user;\n\n-- Product Catalog Service:\
      \ add product data\nINSERT INTO catalog.products (id, name, description, picture,\
      \ price_currency_code, price_units, price_nanos, categories)\nVALUES\n    ('OLJCESPC7Z',\
      \ 'National Park Foundation Explorascope', 'The National Park Foundation''s\
      \ (NPF) Explorascope 60AZ is a manual alt-azimuth, refractor telescope perfect\
      \ for celestial viewing on the go. The NPF Explorascope 60 can view the planets,\
      \ moon, star clusters and brighter deep sky objects like the Orion Nebula and\
      \ Andromeda Galaxy.', 'NationalParkFoundationExplorascope.jpg', 'USD', 101,\
      \ 960000000, 'telescopes'),\n    ('66VCHSJNUP', 'Starsense Explorer Refractor\
      \ Telescope', 'The first telescope that uses your smartphone to analyze the\
      \ night sky and calculate its position in real time. StarSense Explorer is ideal\
      \ for beginners thanks to the app''s user-friendly interface and detailed tutorials.\
      \ It''s like having your own personal tour guide of the night sky', 'StarsenseExplorer.jpg',\
      \ 'USD', 349, 950000000, 'telescopes'),\n    ('1YMWWN1N4O', 'Eclipsmart Travel\
      \ Refractor Telescope', 'Dedicated white-light solar scope for the observer\
      \ on the go. The 50mm refracting solar scope uses Solar Safe, ISO compliant,\
      \ full-aperture glass filter material to ensure the safest view of solar events.\
      \  The kit comes complete with everything you need, including the dedicated\
      \ travel solar scope, a Solar Safe finderscope, tripod, a high quality 20mm\
      \ (18x) Kellner eyepiece and a nylon backpack to carry everything in.  This\
      \ Travel Solar Scope makes it easy to share the Sun as well as partial and total\
      \ solar eclipses with the whole family and offers much higher magnifications\
      \ than you would otherwise get using handheld solar viewers or binoculars.',\
      \ 'EclipsmartTravelRefractorTelescope.jpg', 'USD', 129, 950000000, 'telescopes,travel'),\n\
      \    ('L9ECAV7KIM', 'Lens Cleaning Kit', 'Wipe away dust, dirt, fingerprints\
      \ and other particles on your lenses to see clearly with the Lens Cleaning Kit.\
      \ This cleaning kit works on all glass and optical surfaces, including telescopes,\
      \ binoculars, spotting scopes, monoculars, microscopes, and even your camera\
      \ lenses, computer screens, and mobile devices.  The kit comes complete with\
      \ a retractable lens brush to remove dust particles and dirt and two options\
      \ to clean smudges and fingerprints off of your optics, pre-moistened lens wipes\
      \ and a bottled lens cleaning fluid with soft cloth.', 'LensCleaningKit.jpg',\
      \ 'USD', 21, 950000000, 'accessories'),\n    ('2ZYFJ3GM2N', 'Roof Binoculars',\
      \ 'This versatile, all-around binocular is a great choice for the trail, the\
      \ stadium, the arena, or just about anywhere you want a close-up view of the\
      \ action without sacrificing brightness or detail. It''s an especially great\
      \ companion for nature observation and bird watching, with ED glass that helps\
      \ you spot the subtlest field markings and a close focus of just 6.5 feet.',\
      \ 'RoofBinoculars.jpg', 'USD', 209, 950000000, 'binoculars'),\n    ('0PUK6V6EV0',\
      \ 'Solar System Color Imager', 'You have your new telescope and have observed\
      \ Saturn and Jupiter. Now you''re ready to take the next step and start imaging\
      \ them. But where do you begin? The NexImage 10 Solar System Imager is the perfect\
      \ solution.', 'SolarSystemColorImager.jpg', 'USD', 175, 0, 'accessories,telescopes'),\n\
      \    ('LS4PSXUNUM', 'Red Flashlight', 'This 3-in-1 device features a 3-mode\
      \ red flashlight, a hand warmer, and a portable power bank for recharging your\
      \ personal electronics on the go. Whether you use it to light the way at an\
      \ astronomy star party, a night walk, or wildlife research, ThermoTorch 3 Astro\
      \ Red''s rugged, IPX4-rated design will withstand your everyday activities.',\
      \ 'RedFlashlight.jpg', 'USD', 57, 80000000, 'accessories,flashlights'),\n  \
      \  ('9SIQT8TOJO', 'Optical Tube Assembly', 'Capturing impressive deep-sky astroimages\
      \ is easier than ever with Rowe-Ackermann Schmidt Astrograph (RASA) V2, the\
      \ perfect companion to today''s top DSLR or astronomical CCD cameras. This fast,\
      \ wide-field f/2.2 system allows for shorter exposure times compared to traditional\
      \ f/10 astroimaging, without sacrificing resolution. Because shorter sub-exposure\
      \ times are possible, your equatorial mount won''t need to accurately track\
      \ over extended periods. The short focal length also lessens equatorial tracking\
      \ demands. In many cases, autoguiding will not be required.', 'OpticalTubeAssembly.jpg',\
      \ 'USD', 3599, 0, 'accessories,telescopes,assembly'),\n    ('6E92ZMYYFZ', 'Solar\
      \ Filter', 'Enhance your viewing experience with EclipSmart Solar Filter for\
      \ 8\" telescopes. With two Velcro straps and four self-adhesive Velcro pads\
      \ for added safety, you can be assured that the solar filter cannot be accidentally\
      \ knocked off and will provide Solar Safe, ISO compliant viewing.', 'SolarFilter.jpg',\
      \ 'USD', 69, 950000000, 'accessories,telescopes'),\n    ('HQTGWGPNH4', 'The\
      \ Comet Book', 'A 16th-century treatise on comets, created anonymously in Flanders\
      \ (now northern France) and now held at the Universit\xE4tsbibliothek Kassel.\
      \ Commonly known as The Comet Book (or Kometenbuch in German), its full title\
      \ translates as \"Comets and their General and Particular Meanings, According\

rca_analyses_list.diagnosis: Payment service is instrumented but its OTLP exporter is misconfigured (protocol/endpoint mismatch), preventing traces from reaching the collector. The payment pod is healthy and the otel-collector Service/Endpoints exist, but the payment container sets OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT to "http://$(OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME):4317" while OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL is "grpc", causing the exporter to fail to connect/send (seen as metadata/connection errors in the pod logs).
rca_analyses_list.reasoning:
1) Pod existence/health: payment-6c5f448889-tmxrh is Running and Ready (kubectl describe / get_pods_from_service), so missing traces are not due to absent/unhealthy pods.

4) Collector reachable: otel-collector Service and Endpoints exist and point to an otel collector pod (kubectl get service/endpoints), so the collector itself is present; the failure is in exporter connectivity/configuration, not collector absence.

args.diagnosis: Payment service is instrumented but its OTLP exporter is misconfigured (protocol/endpoint mismatch), preventing traces from reaching the collector. The payment pod is healthy and the otel-collector Service/Endpoints exist, but the payment container sets OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT to "http://$(OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME):4317" while OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL is "grpc", causing the exporter to fail to connect/send (seen as metadata/connection errors in the pod logs).
args.reasoning:
1) Pod existence/health: payment-6c5f448889-tmxrh is Running and Ready (kubectl describe / get_pods_from_service), so missing traces are not due to absent/unhealthy pods.
2) Instrumentation present but misconfigured: pod environment shows OpenTelemetry variables present (OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME=otel-collector, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT="http://$(OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME):4317", OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL="grpc") — a clear mismatch between endpoint scheme (http://) and protocol (grpc) that commonly breaks gRPC exporter connectivity.
3) Exporter errors observed: recent container logs include MetadataLookupWarning / All promises were rejected (UNKNOWN) and other telemetry-related warnings, indicating the SDK/exporter failed to communicate with the collector.
4) Collector reachable: otel-collector Service and Endpoints exist and point to an otel collector pod (kubectl get service/endpoints), so the collector itself is present; the failure is in exporter connectivity/configuration, not collector absence.

Actionable fix: correct OTLP exporter settings in the payment Deployment — either (a) remove the http:// scheme for gRPC (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=otel-collector:4317) when using OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc, or (b) switch protocol to http/protobuf (OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf) if keeping the http:// scheme. After updating, redeploy and confirm traces appear and logs no longer show exporter errors.

message_history.content: Final diagnosis submitted successfully. Investigation complete.

final_report.root_cause: The incident is the result of multiple independent misconfigurations that together produced missing traces and an Envoy runtime warning: (1) frontend-proxy (Envoy) was deployed without an injected bootstrap/config that includes the global downstream connection resource monitor and the checkout cluster/route. The missing global_downstream_max_connections resource monitor produced the explicit connection-limit warning and created a downstream-saturation risk; the absent checkout cluster/route means Envoy is not routing traffic to the checkout service. (2) The checkout application itself is not generating traces (SDK/tracer not initialized) — its pod is configured to export to the collector and the collector is reachable, but no trace spans are emitted. (3) The payment service is instrumented but its OTLP exporter is misconfigured: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set to "http://otel-collector:4317" while OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL="grpc" (HTTP scheme + gRPC protocol mismatch). This causes the payment exporter to fail to deliver traces (manifested as metadata/connection errors in payment logs). Together these explain the observed missing traces (checkout: lack of instrumentation + proxy not routing; payment: exporter misconfiguration) and the Envoy warning/risk of downstream saturation (frontend-proxy misconfiguration).
affected_resources: frontend-proxy-55b6b6c7d9-ljdlz (pod) - Envoy missing global_downstream_max_connections and missing checkout cluster/route
checkout (service) / checkout-6598d86d4b-b9ldc (pod) - no application-level traces generated (SDK/tracer not initialized)
payment (service) / payment-6c5f448889-tmxrh (pod) - OTLP exporter endpoint/protocol mismatch causing exporter failures
Envoy bootstrap/config (missing ConfigMap/volume) - deployment/pod spec shows no mounted Envoy config
otel-collector (service/pod) - collector is present and reachable (impacted only as destination for failing exporters, not root cause)
final_report.evidence_summary: Key evidence supporting the diagnosis: (a) frontend-proxy pod logs contain the explicit Envoy warning: "There is no configured limit to the number of allowed active downstream connections. Configure a limit in `envoy.resource_monitors.global_downstream_max_connections`." Pod spec shows no mounted Envoy config/ConfigMap and minimal memory resource settings. (b) get_services_used_by(frontend-proxy) excluded 'checkout' and inspection of the running proxy configuration/logs found no checkout cluster/route while Kubernetes Service and Endpoints for checkout exist and are healthy — demonstrating a proxy-side missing route. (c) Checkout pod environment includes OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4318 and the otel-collector Service/Endpoints exist; checkout logs contain no exporter/OTLP errors — pointing to lack of instrumentation (no spans generated) rather than network/exporter failure. (d) Payment pod environment shows OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT="http://$(OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME):4317" with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL="grpc", and payment logs contain exporter connection/metadata errors (e.g., MetadataLookupWarning / All promises were rejected (UNKNOWN)) — indicating a scheme/protocol mismatch that prevents gRPC exporter connectivity. (e) otel-collector Service/Endpoints are present and reachable (so collector absence is not the cause).
final_report.investigation_summary: Investigation followed the task priority order: Priority #1 verified Envoy runtime and tracing: Envoy tracing is enabled and returns traces for the proxy, but logs reveal the missing global_downstream_max_connections warning and pod manifest lacks a mounted Envoy config. Priority #2 validated frontend <-> proxy port alignment (no mismatch). Priority #5 discovered frontend-proxy does not have a configured checkout cluster/route even though the checkout Service/Endpoints are healthy. Priority #7 inspected checkout instrumentation: exporter env is configured and collector reachable but no trace spans are emitted, implying missing/disabled instrumentation in the application. Priority #15 inspected payment: pod is instrumented but exporter endpoint/protocol mismatch (http:// + grpc) produced exporter errors in logs; collector reachable. Lower-priority two-sided checks (chatbot, image-provider, other checkout downstreams) remain pending but are not necessary to explain the current missing-trace symptoms identified for checkout and payment. Actions recommended (validated fixes): inject/restore the correct Envoy bootstrap (including resource monitor global_downstream_max_connections and the missing checkout cluster/route) or update deployment so the container image provides the full Envoy config; enable/initialize tracing in the checkout application (add/initialize OpenTelemetry tracer instrumentation); fix payment exporter settings (use otel-collector:4317 without http:// when protocol=grpc, or switch protocol to http/protobuf when keeping http://). After those fixes, verify absence of exporter/log errors and confirm traces appear for checkout and payment.

**Planning Rules**
1. For every symptom, classify the dominant failure domain (app, latency, dependency/config, or platform) and craft a single, testable hypothesis per resource.

3. **Connections (non-negotiable):** Always create at least one task that inspects the connection between every pair of affected resources or the epicenter and its downstream dependents. These tasks must perform explicit two-sided checks (e.g., verify `service-a`'s config for `service-b`'s URL **and** inspect `service-b`'s Kubernetes service definition for the matching port/name) to catch login/URL/port misconfigurations.

**Tool Selection**

**Priority Policy**

- Remaining priorities should rank other high-impact hypotheses (shared dependencies, severe crashes) ahead of narrow or low-scope checks.

4. Stop investigating, even if you have not reached the budget limit, when you have:

5. DO NOT:

prompts_config.supervisor_agent:
You are an expert Site Reliability Engineer analyzing RCA findings to determine the root cause of an incident.

Analyze all symptoms and investigation findings to:
1. Identify patterns and correlations across findings
2. Determine the primary root cause
3. List all affected resources
4. Summarize key evidence

**Understanding Task Priority:**
Each RCA investigation task has been assigned a priority level:
- Priority 1 = Most important / Most likely to reveal root cause (investigated first)
- Priority 2, 3, ... = Progressively lower importance
- Tasks with lower priority numbers should generally have higher weight in your analysis
- The priority reflects the likelihood that investigating that task/resource would uncover the root cause

Use the priority information to contextualize findings: results from priority 1 tasks are typically more significant for determining root cause than lower priority investigations.

**Detection & Localization Requirements:**
- **detection**: Set to `true` if any problem/anomaly was detected in the cluster based on the evidence. Set to `false` only if no issues are found.
- **localization**: Provide a list of ONLY the faulty/problematic components (service names or pod names) directly identified as the root cause. This should be a minimal, precise list - extract ONLY the specific resource(s) that caused the incident, not all affected resources.
  - Example: If a service "user-service" has a misconfiguration causing downstream failures, localization = ["user-service"]
  - Example: If a pod "database-pod-xyz" is failing, localization = ["database-pod-xyz"]
  - Leave empty/null if the root cause cannot be localized to a specific service or pod.

**Root Cause Expectations:**
- Build a causal chain that connects symptoms, investigation evidence, and the precise failure mechanism
- Cite concrete configuration or runtime details (e.g., "service expects port 5432 but database listens on 5433") when diagnosing misconfigurations or integration issues
- If evidence stops at the symptom level, identify the missing proof and pursue it before finalizing

**Strict Iteration Policy:**
Only request another RCA iteration when the existing evidence is insufficient to produce a confident final diagnosis. Never re-run or re-request tasks already marked as completed or currently in progress. When additional work is unavoidable, list only the minimal set of pending task priorities in `tasks_to_be_executed` and clearly justify why each is required. If the current findings support a solid root cause, leave `tasks_to_be_executed` empty and finalize the report.

When you need more evidence, ask for the most targeted pending tasks that can close the causal gap (for example, verifying port mappings, credentials, or configuration values at both ends of a failing connection).

Provide a clear, specific root cause statement that explains what caused the incident and why it happened now.
